=======================================================
 TALJABHAI LILABHAI RABARI  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT =======================================================
Appearance:
MR PR ABICHANDANI with MS POONAM M MAHETA(11265) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR ANVESH V VYAS(5654) for the Respondent(s) No. 1 MR LB DABHI APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 =======================================================

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of notice of rule for respondent - State of Gujarat.

2. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.11217041230159/2023 registered with the Saraswati Police Station, Patan for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471,
409, 120(B) and 201 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that the so-called incident has taken place for the period between 01.01.2019 to 23.06.2021, for which, the FIR has been lodged on 15.04.2023 and the applicant has been arrested in connection with the same on 10.12.2023 and since then, he is in judicial custody.

Learned advocate submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4042/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/03/2024 undefined now the investigation is completed and after submission of the chargesheet, the present application is preferred.
Learned advocate submitted that there is inordinate and unexplained delay caused in filing aforesaid FIR.

Learned advocate submitted that Taljabhai Lilabhai Rabari vs State Of Gujarat on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8737997/
1 FIR has been filed against total 15 accused persons, wherein the applicant is shown as accused no.1.

sentences.text: Learned advocate submitted that it is alleged in the FIR against the applicant that while holding post of President of Melusan Gopalak Sahakari Mangali, the applicant in connivance with other accused persons, has forged the documents including revenue records in the name of persons including the members of the society, who have not applied for loan as also in the name of persons, who have already died and on the strength of said documents, the applicant has applied for loan and misappropriated huge volume of money.
Learned advocate submitted that the co- accused, who is having identical role and/or grave role than the present applicant, has been considered by this Court.
Learned advocate submitted that all the offences are exclusively triable by the Court of Magistrate.

Learned advocate submitted that entire case of the prosecution hinges upon documentary evidence, which have been collected by the IO during the course of investigation and number of witnesses have been cited in the chargesheet and, hence, trial would get delayed.

Learned advocate, under NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4042/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/03/2024 undefined the instructions, submitted that without prejudice to his rights and contentions, the applicant is ready and willing to deposit Rs.13,00,000/- before the concerned trial court, out of which, the applicant will deposit Rs.5,00,000/- within five days from the date of his release and remaining amount of Rs.8,00,000/- will be deposited in four equal installments within four months thereafter i.e. on or before 30the day of each month beginning from April, 2024, May, 2024, June,
2024 and July, 2024 and in support of it, the nephew of the applicant has filed an affidavit narrating the above facts and after the release, the applicant will also file such undertaking.

It is, therefore,
urged that considering the nature of the offence and on the ground of parity, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
4. Learned APP, Mr. Dabhi for the respondent-State as well learned advocate, Mr. Vyas for original complainant have opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
It is submitted that the role of the present applicant is clearly spelt out from the papers of the chargesheet.

Learned APP submitted that in connivance with each other, the accused have committed alleged offences and thereby misappropriated huge volume of amount and the involvement of the present applicant is found out from the chargesheet papers.
Learned APP submitted NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4042/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/03/2024 undefined
that documents have been sent to FSL for verification of the signature but still the said report is awaited.
Learned APP, therefore, urged that considering the gravity and seriousness of the offence the present application may not be entertained.
5. Learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

6. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.
It is found out from the record that the present application is preferred after submission of the chargesheet and now the investigation is completed and the applicant is in jail since 10.12.2023.
All the offences are exclusively triable by the Court of Magistrate.

The case of the prosecution hinges upon documentary evidence, which have been collected by the IO during the course of investigation and number of witnesses have been cited as witness in the chargesheet Taljabhai Lilabhai Rabari vs State Of Gujarat on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8737997/
2 papers and because of which, trial will take considerable time to conclude.

sentences.text: I have considered the role attributed to the present applicant at the time of commission of crime and the role of the co- accused, who has been considered by this Court.

Further as stated above, willingness has been NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4042/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/03/2024 undefined shown by the applicant to deposit Rs.13,00,000/- before the concerned court without prejudice to his rights and contentions.
Therefore considering the above factual aspects and on the ground of parity, the present application deserves to be allowed.

7. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40 as well as in case of Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51.
8.

sentences.text: The authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.

If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the concerned Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4042/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/03/2024 undefined warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.

11. At the trial, the trial Court shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature qua the evidence at this stage made by this Court while enlarging the applicant on bail.
